title: Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi
text:
Bo Ya was a master of the qin, the Chinese zither. Zhong Ziqi was a woodcutter, or in some versions simply a man of no special rank, who was a gifted listener.

When Bo Ya played with his mind on climbing high mountains, Zhong Ziqi would say, "Wonderful! Towering like Mount Tai!" When Bo Ya's thoughts were on flowing water, Zhong Ziqi would say, "Wonderful! Vast and rolling like the great rivers!" Whatever Bo Ya had in his mind as he played, Zhong Ziqi heard it.

Once, the Liezi says, they were caught by a sudden storm and sheltered under a cliff. Bo Ya, feeling melancholy, took up his instrument and played, first a melody of steady rain, then of crashing mountains. With every piece, Zhong Ziqi understood exactly what he meant. Bo Ya put down his qin and sighed that his friend heard what was in his heart, so that nothing he played could escape him.

When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya broke his qin and cut its strings, and he never played again for the rest of his life. He felt there was no one left in the world worth playing for. From this story Chinese has the word zhiyin, "one who knows the tone", for a true friend.
lesson: A friend who truly understands you is rare and precious. Tell such people what they mean to you, and try to be that kind of listener for others.
source: Liezi, Chapter 5 (Tang Wen); Lushi Chunqiu, Book 14 (Ben Wei)
